transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-07 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~64 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Evan (Redwood SE), Nadia (Redwood SE), Maya (Helix MLOps), Carlos (Helix Infra), Priya (Helix Security), Tom (Helix SRE)

Summary (auto): Quick sync to confirm artifact transport process for air-gapped site, verify GPU driver compatibility with our runtime, and scope a short on-prem benchmark.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Samira): Hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
00:07 Speaker 2 (Maya): Yep, loud and clear. Appreciate you taking the time. We're trying to lock down the handoff flow so the on-prem team can apply the bundle without surprises.
00:18 Speaker 1 (Samira): Great. Evan and Nadia from our side will run through the artifact package, the offline activation flow, and then we'll get into driver compatibility. Quick ask — who will be the technical owner on your side for the install?
00:29 Speaker 3 (Carlos): That would be me, Carlos. I'll be on the boots-on-the-ground. I'll coordinate with Tom for the bastion access windows.
00:35 Speaker 1 (Samira): Awesome. Priya, will you be validating the security checklist?
00:38 Speaker 4 (Priya): Yes, I'll own security signoff but we'll need to confirm log collection and KMS key handover for offline activation.
00:45 Speaker 2 (Evan): Quick agenda — artifact manifest, checksum process, offline licensing flow (how keys are delivered and activated without outbound), GPU driver compatibility matrix and fallback, then perf knobs: KV cache warmup, batching, quantization tradeoffs.
00:57 Speaker 5 (Tom): Also want to understand any port requirements for intra-rack traffic and whether the runtime needs time sync or DNS access during activation.
01:05 Speaker 3 (Carlos): And we have some older nodes with A100 40GB and a couple of 80GB gen2, plus an older 2080Ti for dev. We'll send exact kernels.
01:14 Speaker 2 (Evan): Perfect, we'll need exact CUDA and OS versions. On drivers: our runtime supports the latest vendor kernels back to X.Y.Z but there are subtle ABI issues with certain driver patches. We'll share a compatibility matrix — recommended is vendor driver 535.x for the 80GB family, and 470.x for legacy 20-series in restricted mode.
01:30 Speaker 1 (Samira): Note on rollback — we recommend keeping a tested driver snapshot and using our rollback script in the bundle. That avoids partial ABI mismatches during runtime load.
01:42 Speaker 4 (Priya): For offline licensing, is there an HSM or KMS requirement on our end? We can't allow plaintext license files sitting on a host.
01:50 Speaker 2 (Evan): We support encrypted license blobs that you decrypt using your HSM/KMS. We can deliver the blob and a signed activation token that exchanges over the bastion using a one-time challenge. No outbound required. We'll include the verification steps in the runbook.
02:05 Speaker 3 (Carlos): How does the activation failover work — if the bastion window is missed or the token is rejected?
02:10 Speaker 2 (Evan): Good question. There's a grace window baked into the token by default and an offline manual activation procedure where you deliver an activation file generated by our portal — that file is time-stamped and tied to the bundle checksum. We'll document both flows.
02:25 Speaker 6 (Maya): On perf: we care about cold-start latency because our customer-facing APIs spike. What are the expectations for KV warmup and how long until steady-state throughput?
02:33 Speaker 2 (Evan): With our KV cache warmup script, in our benchmarks we see steady-state after 2–3 full prefix passes for typical LLMs — that maps to about 10–30 seconds depending on batch sizes. For your conversational workload, if you run the supplied warmup sequence in the first minute it's usually within 10% of steady-state.
02:54 Speaker 5 (Tom): Do you support prefetching to local NVMe? We're constrained on network egress inside the rack.
03:00 Speaker 2 (Evan): Yes — the runtime supports prefetch to local NVMe with eviction policies and prefers NVMe when available. For air-gapped installs we include a metadata-only manifest that tells the runtime which buckets to seed from the artifact.
03:15 Speaker 3 (Carlos): About batching — our latency SLO is 200ms p95. We can't accept big batching delays. What's the tuning?
03:22 Speaker 2 (Evan): For p95 under 200ms you want small max_batch_size and dynamic batching thresholds with a tight max_latency_ms setting. We prefer continuous batching with adaptive timeouts; for your SLO we'd suggest max_batch_size 8 and max_latency_ms 20–40ms initially, then adjust based on observed token arrival patterns. We'll provide a recommended config.
03:47 Speaker 4 (Priya): Quantization — we have concerns about accuracy drift. If you suggest int8/4-bit, what's the rollback surface?
03:54 Speaker 2 (Evan): We package quantized variants alongside FP16 so you can A/B locally. Quant profiles are pinned in the bundle with a hash; switching back is just a config flip with a couple-second restart to clear KV. We'll include eval prompts so you can measure delta.
04:12 Speaker 1 (Samira): We'll attach a small eval suite for your expected prompts. If regressions exceed thresholds we can auto-fallback to FP16 model at runtime.
04:25 Speaker 6 (Maya): Can you explain the artifact handoff itself — is it a single tarball, signed, with manifest and driver packages?
04:31 Speaker 2 (Evan): Yes, the airgap bundle is a signed tarball with: models/, runtime/, drivers/, checksums.txt (SHA256), license_blob.sig. The drivers/ directory contains vendor-provided driver RPMs or DEBs plus a simple install script that checks kernel modules and blacklists conflicting modules.
04:49 Speaker 3 (Carlos): We sometimes have kernel lockdowns that block module insertion. Any guidance?
04:53 Speaker 2 (Evan): We provide a kernel-compatibility checklist. If module insertions are blocked we ship a driverless mode for inference that uses user-space GPU runtimes where possible, but it has perf tradeoffs. We'll flag those nodes in the manifest.
05:10 Speaker 5 (Tom): For checksum verification, do you expect us to run it in the bastion or on each host?
05:14 Speaker 2 (Evan): The recommended pattern: verify the bundle on the bastion, then transfer artifacts via scp with checksum verification into an isolated staging network, then run per-host verification before install. We'll include the exact commands in the runbook.
05:30 Speaker 4 (Priya): Audit logs — we need a signed attestation of the bundle install and driver install events. Does Redwood produce those?
05:36 Speaker 1 (Samira): Yes, the installation agent emits signed audit lines that you can ship to your SIEM locally. We also log license activation events with the token hash.
05:45 Speaker 6 (Maya): Any gotchas with time sync? Our vaults are strict.
05:49 Speaker 2 (Evan): Activation tokens require clock within 2 minutes. If time sync is restricted, use the manual activation file path. We'll add a step to verify NTP or provide instructions for using hardware time in the runbook.
06:05 Speaker 3 (Carlos): Ok let's talk driver matrix — can you share the exact driver versions you validated?
06:09 Speaker 2 (Evan): We'll share a CSV. Quick tease: for A100 80GB gen2 we validated NVIDIA driver 535.43.x + CUDA 12.1, for 40GB A100 470.159.x in compatibility mode, for the 2080Ti we recommend keeping it isolated as dev only. There are known regressions in 540.x on certain kernels that cause CUDA context hangs — avoid those on prod.
06:34 Speaker 4 (Priya): If we need a signed driver from vendor for FIPS or CC requirements, can that be included?
06:38 Speaker 2 (Evan): Absolutely, include vendor-signed driver packages inside drivers/ and we'll reference them. Our install script will respect vendor signatures and can validate using provided keys.
06:50 Speaker 5 (Tom): Perf tuning — any quick numbers for throughput expected on your runtime for a 13B model on an A100 80GB?
06:57 Speaker 2 (Evan): Rough baseline: unbatched latency ~45–70ms per token depending on seq length; batching increases throughput roughly linearly until memory saturation. For a 13B quantized to 4-bit with KV caching warmed, we see ~3–4 tokens/sec per stream at single-stream steady-state, but your workload will vary. We'll run an on-site microbenchmark to get real numbers.
07:23 Speaker 6 (Maya): About storage — do you expect model shards on NVMe and only KV on RAM?
07:27 Speaker 2 (Evan): Model shards ideally on NVMe, KV cache in GPU DRAM; we also support RAM-backed page cache. For air-gapped installs we recommend at least one NVMe per GPU for local shard staging.
07:40 Speaker 3 (Carlos): What about rolling upgrades for runtime — do you support canary switches?
07:43 Speaker 1 (Samira): Yes, Dedicated and Private modes support canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies. For on-prem you'll run the same control-plane agent in offline mode which can orchestrate local rollouts. We'll show the rollback commands.
07:58 Speaker 4 (Priya): Any regulatory considerations for data residency — we need assurance that no telemetry leaves the air-gapped network.
08:04 Speaker 1 (Samira): We offer a fully air-gapped mode with zero telemetry by default; opt-in telemetry only and can be disabled via config. We'll include the config snippet.
08:15 Speaker 2 (Evan): Quick demo note — we cannot demo the offline install here, but we'll provide a recorded runthrough and a checklist.
08:22 Speaker 6 (Maya): Perfect. For the pilot, timeline — we want a week of validation then a production cut the following week. Is that realistic?
08:28 Speaker 1 (Samira): Yes, if we get GPU inventory and a staging window this week we can ship the bundle and have a 2–3 day install+benchmark, then a 3–4 day validation period.
08:40 Speaker 3 (Carlos): I'll send inventory and proposed windows by Friday.
08:44 Speaker 4 (Priya): We'll also provide our security acceptance criteria doc.
08:49 Speaker 2 (Evan): We'll attach KV warmup and the perf harness; one small note on warmup scripts — avoid running them on the primary prod nodes if you want realistic cold-start behavior. Use a mirrored traffic generator.
09:05 Speaker 5 (Tom): If we hit a driver regression, how quickly can we get a patched runtime?
09:10 Speaker 2 (Evan): Minor patches we can deliver within 48 hours; critical fixes we triage immediately. For air-gapped sites we deliver patched runtime bundles via secure artifact transfer and a delta patcher to reduce bandwidth.
09:25 Speaker 1 (Samira): Alright let's recap next steps and owners.
09:30 Speaker 2 (Evan): Recap — Redwood to share: airgap runbook, driver compatibility CSV, KV warmup script, perf harness, sample eval prompts, and recorded install demo. Helix to share: GPU inventory, OS/kernel versions, security acceptance doc, and preferred bastion windows.
09:50 Speaker 3 (Carlos): Sounds good. We'll target sending inventory by 2026-04-10.
09:56 Speaker 4 (Priya): Security doc by 2026-04-12.
10:00 Speaker 1 (Samira): We'll put a calendar hold for the week of 2026-04-20 for pilot kickoff and send the secure links once the NDA/transfer agreement is signed.
10:10 Speaker 6 (Maya): Thanks everyone.
10:13 Speaker 1 (Samira): Thanks all, will follow up with docs and action items.
